# Capacitor

Native runtime that wraps a web build in a WebView and exposes native capability through plugins. Used
at **7.6.7** in [[farely]] as the Android host, and nowhere else in the source set.

## How Farely uses it

`capacitor.config.json`: appId `com.farely.app`, appName `Farely`, and — the load-bearing line —
`webDir: "../tester/dist"`. The APK does not contain its own web app; it points at the Vite build of
the sibling workspace package. One bundle serves the browser simulator and the phone, which is what
makes [[pure-domain-engine-shared-across-hosts]] possible rather than aspirational.

Native project under `apps/android/android`: AGP 8.7.2, Kotlin Gradle plugin 2.0.21, jvmTarget 21,
Gradle 8.11.1, minSdk 23, compileSdk/targetSdk 36, cordova-android 10.1.1.

## The custom plugin

`FarelyBridgePlugin` is the whole reason Capacitor is here rather than a plain PWA. It carries
`RawOffer` data **out** of the [[android-accessibility-service]] into the WebView, and the verdict back
**in** so `OverlayController` can draw it. Capacitor's plugin surface is the only part of the native
platform the web layer touches directly, besides `CapacitorHttp` — used by `vision.ts` to reach the
[[anthropic-messages-api]] without a browser CORS preflight.

## Why it fits this shape of app

The product is ~12,100 lines of TypeScript UI and domain logic against ~1,099 lines of Kotlin doing
capture and drawing. A framework that treats the web app as primary and native as an extension matches
that ratio. React Native or a fully native rewrite would have inverted it for no gain — the accessibility
service is plain Android code either way, and it is the only genuinely native part.

## Friction it introduces

The gradle project resolves `@capacitor/android` through a relative `../node_modules` path, which makes
the package manager's hoisting layout part of the build contract — the entire subject of
[[pnpm-over-npm-for-capacitor-gradle-path]] and [[pnpm]]. Build chain is two-step and slow:
`vite build` (≈309 kB, with [[maplibre-gl]] split into its own ~1 MB chunk), then `npx cap sync`, then
`gradlew assembleDebug` (4.0 MB debug APK, 6m31s cold).
